title: a cached comment count, first kept by hand and drifting, then kept by a trigger

steps.note: posts carry a comment_count, so the front page doesn't count comments on every view.

steps.sql: SELECT p.id, p.title, p.comment_count, (SELECT count(*) FROM comments AS c WHERE c.post_id = p.id) AS real_count FROM posts AS p ORDER BY p.id
steps.note: the stored count and the real count, side by side.
the app adds a comment and bumps the counter, in one transaction. fine.

steps.sql: SELECT p.id, p.title, p.comment_count, (SELECT count(*) FROM comments AS c WHERE c.post_id = p.id) AS real_count FROM posts AS p ORDER BY p.id

DELETE FROM comments WHERE post_id = 1;
INSERT INTO comments (post_id, body) VALUES (2, 'i am left-handed'), (2, 'me too')
steps.note: a moderation script deletes a comment, and nobody told it about the counter.

steps.sql: SELECT p.id, p.title, p.comment_count, (SELECT count(*) FROM comments AS c WHERE c.post_id = p.id) AS real_count FROM posts AS p ORDER BY p.id
steps.note: post 1 says one comment and has none; post 2 says none and has two. the copy drifted.
a trigger keeps the counter: every insert or delete on comments adjusts it, in the same transaction. then a one-time fix of the drift.

steps.sql: SELECT p.id, p.title, p.comment_count, (SELECT count(*) FROM comments AS c WHERE c.post_id = p.id) AS real_count FROM posts AS p ORDER BY p.id

INSERT INTO comments (post_id, body) VALUES (1, 'first!'), (1, 'second');
DELETE FROM comments WHERE body = 'me too'
steps.note: the same careless script again: two inserts, one delete, no counter code anywhere.

steps.sql: SELECT p.id, p.title, p.comment_count, (SELECT count(*) FROM comments AS c WHERE c.post_id = p.id) AS real_count FROM posts AS p ORDER BY p.id
steps.note: the trigger fired once per row. the counts agree.
